organization.export.glossary.amounts: net_amount, subtotal, tax_total, total — before tax, the tax, and the total owed or credited, tax included.
organization.export.glossary.audit: action, resource_type, resource_id, payload — in audit_log.csv, what happened, named for the thing and then the event (user.created, invoice.issued), what it happened to, and its details as JSON. The app’s Audit log shows each in words.
organization.export.glossary.created: created_at, updated_at — when the record was made and last changed, in UTC.
organization.export.glossary.dates: invoice_date, due_date, credit_date — the days the document carries.
organization.export.glossary.direction: direction — on an order, sale or purchase.
organization.export.glossary.flags: A column starting is_ holds true or false, such as is_active.
organization.export.glossary.id: id — the record’s own id. A column ending in _id elsewhere holds it: partner_id is an id in partners.csv.
organization.export.glossary.intro: Each line names a column, or a family of columns, and says what it holds. A column in several files means the same in each.
organization.export.glossary.issued: issued_at, voided_at, void_reason — when the document was issued, when it was voided, and why.
organization.export.glossary.language: language, second_language — the languages the document prints in: en, fr-CA or zh-Hans.
organization.export.glossary.lots: lot_id, code, expires_at — a lot of goods, the code printed on it, and the day it expires.
organization.export.glossary.movements: from_location_id, to_location_id, reason — in stock_movements.csv, where stock left, where it arrived, and why.
organization.export.glossary.number: number — the number printed on the document, such as INV-000001 or CN-000001.
organization.export.glossary.numbering: document_numbering, document_sequences — how each kind of document is numbered, and the counter for each year, month or day; a number already given stays on its document.
organization.export.glossary.organizatio: organization_id — the organization. The same in every row.
organization.export.glossary.parties: seller_…, bill_to_…, ship_to_… — the seller, the customer billed and where the goods went: names and addresses as the document printed them that day.
organization.export.glossary.price: unit_price — the price of one unit, before tax. currency — its three-letter code, such as CAD or CNY.
organization.export.glossary.quantity: quantity_ordered, quantity_fulfilled, quantity_returned — how many were ordered, shipped or received, and returned.
organization.export.glossary.reference: reference — on an order, the customer’s or supplier’s own number for it.
organization.export.glossary.sku: sku — the code of a product variant, as on its label.
organization.export.glossary.status: status — where the record stands, such as draft, confirmed, issued or voided.
organization.export.glossary.title: Glossary: what the columns mean
organization.export.glossary.who: created_by, issued_by, voided_by, actor_id — who did it: a user_id in members.csv.
organization.export.readme.documents: The documents folder holds every invoice ever issued, voided ones included, and every credit note, each as a PDF named by its number, exactly as Download PDF gives it. A draft is not there: it was never sent.
organization.export.readme.files: The files folder holds every file in use, such as the logo and product images, named by its id in files.csv and its original name.
organization.export.readme.members: members.csv lists the members, with the user_id that columns such as created_by and actor_id hold. Someone who is no longer a member appears by id only. role_permissions.csv lists what each role may do. organization.csv holds the organization’s own details and settings, and audit_log.csv its audit log.
organization.export.readme.snapshot: Every file shows the organization as it was when the export began.
organization.export.readme.tables: Each .csv file is one kind of record, named for its table, with a row per record and every column as stored. Ids join the files: a column ending in _id holds the id of a row in another file, such as invoice_id in invoice_lines.csv, which is an id in invoices.csv.
organization.export.readme.title: {organization}: everything it holds, exported {date}
organization.export.readme.values: Quantities and money are written as stored, with a full stop for the decimal point. Days are written YYYY-MM-DD, and moments YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, in UTC.

roles.description.owner: Everything, including costs, issuing invoices, settings and closing the organization.
roles.description.viewer: Looks at orders, stock and invoices, and changes nothing.
